Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy with feeding difficulties and abdominal distension; tell me, does your vomiting contain bile, which looks like greenish fluid?

Also, please tell me if your belly looks like it has ridges or if you pass gas frequently.

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dilated bowel segments with absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the X-ray results showing dilated bowel segments and an absence of rectal gas, which strongly suggests an obstruction. Has your baby ever passed meconium within the first 48 hours of life?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Distal Intestinal Obstruction (likely Meconium Ileus or Distal Intestinal Obstruction Syndrome). Given the age, feeding difficulties, bilious vomiting (if present), and X-ray showing dilated bowel with no rectal gas, this is consistent with a distal obstruction. If no meconium was passed in the first 48 hours, meconium ileus is highly likely; if meconium was passed but symptoms started later, consider other causes like atresia or volvulus. Please confirm whether meconium was passed in the first 48 hours and whether the vomiting is bilious.
